title: About Sephiria Guide
description: About sephiria-guide.com — an unofficial English fan guide for Sephiria 1.0 by Team Horay.
meta: Unofficial fan guide · Not affiliated with Team Horay · Last updated: 2026-11-10
body:
sephiria-guide.com is an unofficial English fan guide for Sephiria (Team Horay). It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by the developer or publisher, and it is not an official wiki.

The site is written and maintained by one person, Jerome (GitHub @Jeromelll), who can be reached at jeromell@be-winner.com. There is no editorial team, no freelance pool and no sponsor deciding what gets covered. Pages are added when a question keeps coming up in search and the current answers are incomplete, contradictory or written for an older build.

What the site covers

  • Beginner guide — the run loop, Side Bag rules, early unlocks, and which habits transfer.
  • Builds and the Companion build — how weapon paths and Artifact families combine, with the version limits stated.
  • Weapons and upgrades — the six branches, how upgrade offers work, and the evolution routes players finish.
  • Destiny Inscription and the Wishing Fountain — the permanent tree and the town Artifact picker.
  • Hard Mode — the Root’s Retreat unlock and the outdated path that still circulates.
  • Artifacts and Tablets — inventory geometry, bond pairings, and why an inactive slot is dead weight.
  • Bosses, co-op, multiplayer setup, secret rooms, costumes and the scythe clarification.

The guide index lists every Sephiria guide page on the site, so nothing is reachable only through a search result.

Why it exists

Sephiria answers are not hard to find; current answers are. Search results mix pre-release advice, Early Access screenshots and full-release changes, and a guide that was correct in 2025 can send you to a menu that no longer exists. The Hard Mode unlock is the clearest example: older guides still route players to a Destiny node that was replaced by a village dialogue. Pages that depend on a specific patch say which build they describe, and where a question could not be settled the page says so instead of filling the gap with a guess.

How claims are sourced and hedged

Guide pages are built from public material: the Steam store listing, official patch notes and news posts, Steam discussions, achievement lists, dated community guides, and videos used for route shapes rather than exact numbers. Where first-hand play settles a question, it is used and described as such. Every article page ends with a Sources list naming what was checked.

Claims are graded rather than blended. Facts from official posts are stated plainly. Community-reported figures are labelled as reports and paired with the instruction to confirm them in-game — fountain capacity and rarity costs are the obvious cases, because those numbers move between patches. When two sources disagree, the disagreement stays visible, as it does on the costumes page for unlock conditions. One player's clear is never presented as a guaranteed result.

What this site is not

  • Not official, and not connected to Team Horay. Questions about the game itself belong with the developer or Steam Support.
  • Not a datamining project. Nothing here comes from extracted game files, unreleased builds or leaked content; if a detail is not visible in the public client or a public post, it is not on the site.
  • Not a file host. No mods, trainers, saves, cheats or downloads are distributed here.
  • Not a paid placement service. Guide pages carry no sponsored sections, and advertising does not decide coverage.

How to report an error

Send the page URL, the sentence that is wrong, and what you saw in-game instead, ideally with a patch note, Steam post or dated guide that can be re-checked. Corrections that come with a source get applied fastest. The contact page explains what to include and what to expect; the editorial policy describes how updates and corrections are handled.

How to use the site

  1. Start with the beginner guide if you have not finished the story route. It covers the systems that every other page assumes.
  2. Pick your next task, not your next topic: unlocking Hard Mode, fixing a build, or finding a room all point to different pages.
  3. Read the version line and the Sources list before acting on a number. If a figure is labelled as community-reported, check it in your client first.
  4. When a page says it cannot confirm something, treat that as the boundary of what the site knows rather than an invitation to guess.

Other guides on this domain

The same domain also carries a separate Football Manager 27 guide section maintained by the same person, plus a few legacy pages for other games kept only so old links still resolve. Those pages follow the same sourcing rules but are outside the scope of this Sephiria guide.

Contact: Contact page · jeromell@be-winner.com. See also Privacy and Editorial policy.
